new_scholarship.name: KAUST Fellowship
new_scholarship.program_type: University graduate fellowship (award is automatic on admission)
new_scholarship.official_source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
new_scholarship.description: KAUST states that all admitted students receive the benefits of the KAUST Fellowship, which supports them for the duration of their graduate studies. The published package is full tuition support, a monthly living allowance of USD 20,000-30,000 a year depending on qualifications and progression, housing, medical and dental coverage, and relocation support; charges may apply to dependent housing and dependent medical and dental coverage. There is no separate fellowship application: funding is granted through admission to a KAUST master's, MS/PhD or PhD programme. Applications for the Fall 2027 intake opened on 28 September 2026 and close on 3 January 2027.

new_scholarship.name: Arab Fund Fellowship for Academic Excellence (برنامج الزمالات للتميز الأكاديمي)
new_scholarship.official_source: Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development (AFESD)
new_scholarship.description: Run since 1997 by the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development, the Fellowship for Academic Excellence sends Arab PhD holders to prestigious foreign universities to conduct advanced research and/or teach. The Fund states that since its inception the programme has awarded about 191 fellowships to Arab researchers of different nationalities and fields. Support is described as full: a fixed maintenance allowance, round-trip airfare for the beneficiary and eligible family members, and health and personal accident insurance for the whole stay. The grant is usually awarded for twelve months, with shorter periods considered only in very special cases, and applications are accepted on a continuous basis provided they reach the Fund at least a year before the intended start date at the host university.

new_scholarship.application_period: Continuous intake; applications must be submitted at least one year before the expected starting date of the stay at the foreign university
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to Arab PhD holders who have not previously received an Arab Fund fellowship. The Fund describes the fellowship as a bridge for outstanding Arab Ph.D. holders to lecture or conduct advanced research at world-renowned universities.

Intended activity is advanced research and/or teaching at a foreign university

The official pages do not publish the value of the maintenance allowance, so no funding figure is recorded. The official page also points to Bibliotheca Alexandrina's list of other higher-education funding opportunities, which is not part of this award.

programme_detail_official.description: The Fellowship for Academic Excellence is the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development's own post-doctoral research and teaching fellowship. Operating since 1997, it has awarded about 191 fellowships to Arab researchers across nationalities and fields of specialisation, funding research and lecturing at prestigious foreign universities. The Fund describes the support as full financial support consisting of a fixed maintenance allowance, round-trip airfare for the beneficiary and eligible family members, and health and personal accident insurance for the duration of the stay. Awards normally run for twelve months and applications are accepted continuously on the condition that they arrive at least a year before the intended start of the stay.

new_scholarship.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo
new_scholarship.official_source: The American University in Cairo (AUC), in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation
new_scholarship.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC is a fully packaged graduate fellowship for African students, starting with the Spring 2027 cohort, under which AUC intends to award fellowships to 300 graduate students in fields that promote African economic development. It targets academically talented young Africans with leadership potential who face the highest economic and social barriers. The award is granted for the total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment, subject to review every semester for satisfactory academic performance, and it covers tuition, a stipend, a laptop, health insurance, university accommodation, local transport and, for fellows who do not already reside in Egypt, roundtrip airfare. Application requires two separate steps: the AUC graduate application and a dedicated Mastercard Foundation Scholars application.
new_scholarship.duration: Total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment, reviewed every semester for satisfactory academic performance
new_scholarship.application_period: Spring 2027 cycle: applications open 7 October 2026 and close 2 November 2026 (deadlines page last updated 23 August 2026). Fall 2027 Cycle 1 opens 22 December 2026 and closes 17 January 2027; Fall 2027 Cycle 2 opens 6 April 2027 and closes 6 May 2027.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be residing in an African country and hold citizenship of at least one African country, be aged 35 or younger at the time of application, be new graduate degree-seeking students meeting AUC graduate admissions requirements (transfers are not eligible), hold a bachelor's degree with a minimum overall GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent, and demonstrate financial need.

programme_detail_official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC is a graduate fellowship for African students that starts with the Spring 2027 cohort and is intended to award fellowships to 300 graduate students in fields that promote African economic development. AUC states the programme is for academically talented young individuals with leadership potential who face the highest economic and social barriers. Awards are made for the total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment and are reviewed every semester for satisfactory academic performance. Coverage published by AUC comprises tuition fees for nine credits per semester, a fall and spring stipend, a laptop, student services and activities fees, medical service and health insurance, university accommodation, an AUC bus subscription or travel allowance, possible coverage of remedial English modules, roundtrip airfare for fellows not residing in Egypt, and possible extra funding for research, publications, conference attendance and disability-related software. Applicants must submit both the AUC graduate application and a separate Mastercard Foundation Scholars application, and fellows must keep full-time status, a 3.2 minimum GPA, complete 12 hours per week of related academic work, respond to reporting requests and attend programme workshops.

FLAGGED FOR MERGE: this record and the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo in this same file are two host institutions of one Mastercard Foundation umbrella scheme. They are submitted separately because the awarding body is the host university in each case, because each partner runs its own cohort with its own deadline and its own selection through its own portal (University of Rwanda: mcfsprecruitment.ur.ac.rw; AUC: aucegypt.edu), and because they open different countries and degree levels (Rwanda undergraduate, Egypt graduate). rejected.candidate: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) Scholarship, Qatar
rejected.reason: Fails the fully-funded test. HBKU's own scholarship page states students are responsible for covering housing from their stipend or personal funds, that HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing, that scholarships are not guaranteed and are awarded only on a merit or need basis, and lists partial tuition waivers by programme (for example 75% for STEM MS, 60% for SHAPE MS, 0% for LL.M.). Graduate admissions opened 1 October 2026 with an international deadline of 1 February 2027, so the record is current, but it is not a fully funded award.

The only dated schedules on the programs page are stale 2023-2024 module dates. Separately, the only logo published by the site (https://www.qatarscholarships.qa/logo.svg) is fill #FFFFFF throughout, i.e. a white-on-transparent wordmark, which the brief bans. Two independent disqualifiers, so not submitted.
